description: During plaud-ingest step-01, invoking the plaud-discover skill via a background fork (Skill tool) produced an incorrect discovery result: it reported all 129 files in ~/Downloads/transcript-staging as 'unprocessed' and recommended ingesting all 129, writing this to systems/eval-harness/skill-runs/plaud-discover-latest.json. This contradicted the previously verified state (only 1-2 genuinely new recordings; ~120+ staging files are pre-existing already-ingested duplicates flagged for cleanup in an earlier session). The fork appears to have listed the local staging folder and treated file presence there as 'unprocessed', skipping the documented API-vs-vault file_id dedup step in skills/plaud-discover/SKILL.md (Plaud API enumeration via /file/simple/web + Obsidian vault frontmatter file_id scan under zzPlaud/).
correction: Manually re-ran discovery correctly: called fetch_plaud.py's list_recordings() directly against the live Plaud API (129 total recordings) and cross-referenced against a live Obsidian dataview scan of zzPlaud/**/*.md frontmatter file_id fields (128 unique ids). True diff = exactly 2 new recordings (9655c434b58437e56c3c80e441d541d9 and 2206973163d38abccd15da29b0ec7b60), both already ready for fetch. Did not act on the fork's false 129-file recommendation.
failure_mode: Background/forked skill execution deviated from the skill's documented procedure (skipped vault dedup, used staging-folder listing as a proxy for 'new'), producing a plausible-looking but incorrect result that would have caused mass re-ingestion of ~127 already-ingested duplicate notes if trusted without verification.
systemic_fix: Consider flagging plaud-discover for rigby-skill-audit / rigby-skill-reflect: the skill's fork-execution path needs stronger enforcement that vault dedup (step 3 of skills/plaud-discover/SKILL.md) actually runs, not just staging-folder enumeration. Also consider having the skill write its dedup method into its completion artifact (skill-runs/*.json) so downstream consumers can sanity-check whether the vault cross-reference actually occurred.
